newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGB FUTURES CREEP HIGHER TO END TOKYO DAY FIRMER.
newsitem.headline: JGB FUTURES CREEP HIGHER TO END TOKYO DAY FIRMER.

text.p: The benchmark September 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract ended thin Wednesday Tokyo trade slightly higher, but the upside remained heavy around 126.50 and traders said consolidation at current levels was likely for the rest of the week.

A flurry of buying emerged just prior to the close to help lift key September, but this was little more than a reaction to September's failure to weaken once the Nikkei stock average crept back above 19,000, one trust bank trader said.
September ended the day at 126.48, up 0.07 from Tuesday's close, with turnover a light 29,179 contracts.

September drifted as low as 126.24 in morning trade on bearish sentiment carried over from Tuesday, when banks were detected selling medium- to longer-termed bonds, traders said. They added, however, that buy-backs of these securities in the afternoon helped lend futures modest support.

Light buying of the 190-series cash bonds emerged in afternoon trade, partly on a sense that they were relatively cheap compared with the benchmark 182nd bond. But with most investors sidelined due to summer holidays, activity was lethargic and failed to give either cash bonds or futures a significant boost, one city bank trader said.
The yield on the benchmark 182nd cash bond was at 2.125 percent at 0619 GMT against 2.130 percent at Tuesday's close.
Traders said that, while the topside would remain heavy from 126.50 on up, significant resistance was not seen until 127.00, a key psychological point.
But traders said it was unlikely that anything strong enough to lift bonds that far would emerge for the rest of the week.
"We're looking at consolidation around current levels," one trust bank trader said.
